描述_ZN: Listening to the Pines" scroll, painted by Xiang Shengmo in the Qing Dynasty, on paper with ink brush, 138.5 cm in length and 60 cm in width.　　This painting is inscribed with the following title: "Occasionally, I came here to find a deer trail, and I sat listening to the pine breeze, which was also refreshing. When I was staying in the western suburbs of Jiangcheng on the day of the Geng Yin Highlander, I liked these two words and made up the picture with a sudden stroke. Xiang Shengmu." Inscription: "Xushan Woodcutter Xiang Bozi" and other seals. "Geng Yin" refers to the seventh year of Shunzhi in the Qing Dynasty (1650), when Xiang was 54 years old. The ancient custom of the Chrysanthemum Festival is to "ascend the heights". According to the title, it can be seen that this picture is Xiang's in the seventh year of the reign of Shunzhi festival and friends climbing high for the chanting of good lines and painting.　　The work is painted with cloudy cliffs and fog, long pines and gnarled branches, and a high priest chanting at the stream. The brushwork of the trees and rocks is thick and calm, the lines of the figures are round and simple, and the mood is clear and ancient, typical of Xiang Shengmo's landscape figure paintings.
